blocks.text: Albion homes listed and sold, June to September 2026

Albion, September 2026. Detached houses: 62 listed at month end and 6 sold in September, a sales ratio of 10% (a buyers’ market). Condos and townhomes: 18 listed at month end and 4 sold in September, a sales ratio of 22% (a sellers’ market).

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 23 sold over 4 months against an average of 58.5 listed, about 10.2 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 9 sold. Condos and townhomes: 15 sold over 4 months against an average of 19.5 listed, about 5.2 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 5 sold.

faq.q: How did Albion sell in September 2026?
faq.a: Actively by Maple Ridge standards: detached recorded 62 active listings, 6 solds and a 10% sales ratio — the second-highest detached sales count in the city — while Condos & Townhomes recorded 18 listings, 4 solds and a 22% sales ratio, the city's second-highest attached ratio (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

Albion Elementary (10031 240 Street), c'usqunela Elementary (24093 104 Avenue) and Samuel Robertson Technical Secondary (10445 245 Street) are in the area, with Kanaka Creek Elementary (11120 234a Street) at its west edge — addresses per the BC Ministry K-12 school file; catchments are address-specific, so check any address in the SD42 School Locator.

faq.q: What did the 2025 Albion Area Plan update change?
faq.a: Council adopted the update on October 28, 2025: it enhances walking and cycling connections, supports growth of local commercial nodes, introduces buffers where urban development meets farmland, and consolidates land-use policies to reflect provincial housing legislation.

faq.q: Can a house here have a suite or more units?
faq.a: One secondary suite per lot inside the single detached building, up to 40% of the building's gross floor area and not in the floodplain area; eligible single-detached and duplex lots may also have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws.
